facts.title: Casey & Company LLC
facts.agency: Department of the Interior, National Park Service
facts.solicitation: RFQ No. 140P1326Q0029 (leaf removal services, Rock Creek National Park)
facts.procurement_type: Commercial services; small business set-aside under RFO part 12 procedures
facts.evaluation_scheme: Lowest-priced technically acceptable quotation; price was the sole evaluation factor
facts.background: On June 26, 2026, NPS issued a small business set-aside RFQ for leaf removal services at Rock Creek National Park under RFO part 12 commercial procedures. The RFQ contemplated a fixed-price purchase order with a one-year base period, four one-year options, and a six-month extension option. Price was the sole evaluation factor, and award was to go to the responsible vendor offering the lowest price. Vendors were to email quotations to the contracting officer's designated address by 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on July 29, and the solicitation placed responsibility for timely delivery on offerors. Casey states it emailed its quotation on July 23 and received a delivery confirmation indicating the message reached a mail server. By the July 29 closing date, the contracting officer had received 15 quotations, including Brann's, but none from Casey. NPS selected Brann Services and posted the award notice on SAM on August 11. That day Casey requested a debriefing and attached its quotation; on August 12 the contracting officer stated he had no record of receiving a quotation from Casey and declined to consider it. An internal IT investigation found that the July 23 email reached the agency's email system, was flagged as a high-confidence phishing message, and was quarantined without reaching the contracting officer's inbox. Casey filed an agency-level protest, which NPS denied on August 27, and then protested to GAO.

protester_grounds.claim: The agency improperly refused to consider Casey's quotation, which Casey contends was timely submitted to the designated address and was received by the agency's email server before the deadline.

The agency knew its email system had previously quarantined legitimate quotations and unreasonably failed to correct this known problem, so the quarantine reflects a systemic failure requiring consideration of Casey's quotation and a new award decision.

facts.agency_position: NPS argues that Casey's quotation never reached the contracting officer's designated email address because the anti-spam system quarantined it, so it was not timely received and the agency properly declined to consider it. NPS contends that receipt by the agency's email gateway does not constitute receipt at the designated address. The agency characterizes the quarantine as an isolated loss rather than a systemic failure, noting that the other quarantined messages were automated notifications from a different sender that the contracting officer did not know about before award. NPS also argues that the contracting officer's reference to a prior quarantine in a separate procurement does not show a systemic problem.
facts.record_facts_protected: Casey's transmission trace shows its quotation email was sent July 23 at 8:59 a.m. ET and delivered to a recipient mail server. The agency's quarantine record lists the email as received by the server but not released to the recipient's address. All 15 other vendors that submitted quotations had their quotations received in the contracting officer's inbox by the closing date, and one of those was received 27 minutes late and was considered. In the weeks before the due date, the agency's anti-spam program quarantined 16 automated third-party notifications sent to the agency from Casey's service platform, and the contracting officer was not aware of them before award. The contracting officer was aware of a prior quarantine of a quotation in a separate procurement, where that contracting officer received 27 other quotations without issue. The record contains no evidence of a deliberate effort by contracting personnel to prevent an award to Casey.
